beats.text: Five Stoic lessons on money and wealth.
One. Wealth isn't having the most. It's having enough — and knowing that you do.
Two. Money is a tool, not a scoreboard. It can buy comfort; it can't buy character or calm.
Three. Seneca was rich, but held it loosely — ready, any day, to hand it all back without flinching.
Four. Use fortune; never trust it. What luck gives, luck can take back overnight.
Five. The best things — time, peace, good people, a clear conscience — were never for sale.
Chase enough, not endless. The richest person, the Stoics said, is the one who needs the least.
